To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the semantic-identification principle of causal reasoning can be implemented by a Causal Semantic model, which is a generative model with a latent variable for the variation factor, 2) the model can be learned efficiently by a novel design in Variational Bayes, 3) the model can predict the output of OOD examples by a novel design for OOD prediction, and 4) the semantic- identification principle guarantees the boundedness and adaptability of OOD prediction.
(a) CSG can identify semantic factor by fitting data; (b) CSG can predict out-of-distribution examples; and (c) CSG can generalize to out-of-distrbution data with bounded error.

(1) CSG learns a causal semantic representation by separating the semantic factor from the variation factor in the training data, and (2) the learned semantic representation is invariant to the variation factor and hence can be generalized to OOD domains, and (3) CSG can adapt to OOD domains by learning the variation factor from the OOD data.

we propose a novel causal generative model, CSG, for learning causal representation from data, and develop a novel OOD prediction method based on CSG, which can achieve better OOD performance.
